hints: Calculate the driving force from the given power output $120\text{ kW} = 120000\text{ W}$ at speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $D = \frac{P}{v}$.
Since the speed remains constant as the lorry ascends the hill, acceleration is zero, so driving force balances the sum of the resistance force and the component of weight down the slope.
Set up the equilibrium equation $D - R - mg \sin \alpha^\circ = 0$ and solve for the angle $\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the forward driving force from power $P = 120\text{ kW} = 120000\text{ W}$ at speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{120000}{20} = 6000\text{ N}$$

Since the lorry ascends at constant speed, acceleration is zero, so forces parallel to the incline balance:
$$D - R - mg \sin \alpha^\circ = 0$$
$$6000 - 1600 - 18000(10)\sin \alpha^\circ = 0$$
$$4400 = 180000 \sin \alpha^\circ$$
teacher_walkthrough: When the lorry ascends the incline at a constant speed of $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$).

Step 1: Calculate the forward driving force $D$:
$$P = 120\text{ kW} = 120000\text{ W}$$
$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{120000}{20} = 6000\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Identify opposing forces along the incline:
1. Constant resistance to motion: $R = 1600\text{ N}$.
2. Component of the lorry's weight down the incline: $W_{\parallel} = mg \sin \alpha^\circ = 18000 \times 10 \times \sin \alpha^\circ = 180000 \sin \alpha^\circ$.

Step 3: Apply equilibrium parallel to the road:
$$D - R - mg \sin \alpha^\circ = 0$$
$$6000 - 1600 - 180000 \sin \alpha^\circ = 0$$
$$4400 = 180000 \sin \alpha^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Calculates driving force $D = 6000\text{ N}$, resolves parallel to the hill $6000 - 1600 - 180000\sin \alpha^\circ = 0$, and evaluates $\alpha = 1.40^\circ$.
